answer: Trust propagation with graph locality resists sybil attacks. Voting weight is personalized PageRank from a kernel of established seed identities, so influence flows only along verified interaction edges. A clone farm looks brilliant from inside, like an opal of mutual approvals, yet it sits on a remote knoll of the trust graph: its internal edges carry no external trust, so incoming weight is capped by the few honest links it can build. Since seeds rate-limit and audit each handshake, every clone needs genuine service contracts with established peers -- linear cost, no multiplicative return.
